Resolves #18529

The dock catalog's `kind` is gone — removed from `WorkspaceDocument.dockZoneItemKeys` outright, with no allowlist entry, no read-side tolerance and no deprecation window. No engine code ever read it, and its values named nothing the dock instantiates: every pane carrying `kind: 'panel'` is a `component.Base`, and `container.Panel` appears zero times across `examples/dashboard` and `apps/workstation`. On the authored surface it was already a ratified avoided-trap from #18474, agreed on Discussion #18468 before any code, and the merged example carried it ten times. Two preservation shapes were proposed on the ticket and both withdrawn: keeping it read-only (circular — a pinned engine SHA already supplies that decoupling) and relocating to `metadata` (a value that names nothing just becomes noise in a nicer box).

Evidence: L3 (both CI-gating tiers run locally and unfiltered — `unit` 3722/3722, `components` 268/268, both exit 0) → L3 required (AC-1b, AC-2 and AC-4 are all validation-observable through the allowlist). Residual: AC-3, Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#120.

## Deltas from ticket

**AC-3 is proposed as a fold, not a separate filing.** The ticket says "its own ticket in its own repo". `CockpitDockDocument.mjs` carries `componentRef` and `kind` **on the same lines**, and #120 already owns that file for the same engine SHA bump — two tickets would mean two PRs conflicting on identical text. Proposed on #120 and left to its author; if she prefers separation I file what AC-3 literally asks for.

**The break is smaller than the ticket estimated, in the removal's favour.** #18529 treats the rejecting allowlist as a real cost absorbed by consumers. Nothing has ever shipped a `neo.dock.zone.v1` document — it is on neither `main` nor npm `13.1.0`, which carries an older flat dock with no `SCHEMA` constant and no durable writer. Established while #18537 was closed as a false premise.

**ADR 0029 and `DockZoneModel.md` are updated here**, since both described `kind` as part of the item record.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI.

The one thing a green suite cannot show, so it is recorded here: **the sweep's own safety argument.** Seven distinct fields in this repo are named `kind`, and only the catalog's is dead — `placement.kind` (`tab-*`/`split-*`/`edge-*`, read by `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:853`, `Operations.mjs:716`, `PreviewProducer.mjs`) is live drag geometry, plus `RETIREMENT_KINDS`, transaction descriptors, render-queue entries, link-checker targets and one blog prose sample.

A **denylist** on placement prefixes is unsafe and the first pass proved it: `History.spec.mjs:59`'s `{kind: 'split', payload: {…}}` is a transaction descriptor with no dash and slipped straight through, giving 275 removals where only 246 are ours — 29 sites across six unrelated subsystems. The sweep was inverted to **allowlist** the six confirmed catalog values *and* require a catalog marker (`title`, `reference`, `header`, or a policy flag) on the line or inside a bounded ±6-line window. The auditable check is the complement: the preserved set contains **no** catalog value.

Mutation-adjacent control: the round-trip generator seeded `kind` **programmatically** (`if (random() < 0.5) record.kind = 'panel'`), invisible to any literal sweep, and turned red the moment the allowlist entry went. That red is the proof the removal reaches validation rather than merely deleting text.
